title: Interpretability and AI alignment
stage: Graduate study and research in machine learning
audience: a graduate preparing for research in machine learning, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Learn the research fields that try to understand what models compute and to make them reliably do what people intend: feature attribution, probing and its pitfalls, mechanistic interpretability (features, circuits, induction heads, superposition and sparse dictionary learning), adversarial robustness, the alignment problem (specification gaming, reward hacking and goal misgeneralization), learning from human feedback and its limits, scalable oversight, evaluations and red-teaming, and the governance of advanced AI, with open problems and disagreements among researchers presented fairly.
primary_reading: Interpretable Machine Learning by Christoph Molnar (free online)

weeks.2: Feature attribution: gradients, integrated gradients and Shapley values
weeks.8: The alignment problem: specification gaming, reward hacking and goal misgeneralization
weeks.9: Learning from human feedback and its limits
weeks.10: Scalable oversight: debate, recursive reward modeling and AI feedback
weeks.12: Governance of advanced AI and open research problems

blocks.deliverable: Compute attributions for a small model by hand and in code.
Train a linear probe on supplied activations.
Analyze a toy model in which features share dimensions.
Week 7 midterm; craft an adversarial perturbation for a linear classifier.
Analyze a failure of a learned reward model.
Write a research proposal on one open problem.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Interpretability or alignment mini-project: choose one supplied option (find a circuit in a small network whose weights are supplied, train a sparse autoencoder on supplied activations, or demonstrate reward hacking in a small supplied reinforcement learning environment), run the experiment, and write a workshop-style paper with a clear claim, evidence, limitations and the strongest alternative explanation of your results.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
